name: Parmenas
source_summary: One of the seven men chosen by the Jerusalem church, full of the Spirit and wisdom, to oversee the daily distribution of food to widows, freeing the apostles for prayer and preaching.
family_friendly_summary: As the early church in Jerusalem grew larger, a problem came up: some widows were being overlooked when food was shared out each day. To fix this fairly, the apostles asked the whole church to choose seven trustworthy men, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, to take charge of this important job so the apostles could focus on prayer and teaching. Parmenas was one of the seven men chosen. The church prayed for these men, and the apostles laid hands on them, setting them apart for this service. We aren't told anything more about Parmenas individually, but being chosen for this role meant the whole church trusted him to serve fairly and faithfully.
adult_story: Parmenas appears once, named among the seven men the Jerusalem church selected to resolve a dispute in Acts 6. Greek-speaking (Hellenistic) believers had complained that their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food, compared to Hebrew-speaking widows (Acts 6:1). Rather than neglect either preaching or practical care, the apostles instructed the congregation to select seven men "of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom" to oversee the distribution, freeing the apostles to devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word (6:2-4). The church chose Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas -- all bearing Greek names, likely reflecting the very community whose needs had been overlooked. The apostles prayed and laid hands on them, formally commissioning them (6:6). Nothing further is recorded of Parmenas individually; unlike Stephen and Philip, whose subsequent ministries Acts narrates at length, Parmenas's name appears only in this list. His inclusion still matters: the early church entrusted a practical, servant-hearted task to men marked by spiritual character, not status, and the arrangement "pleased the whole congregation" (6:5).
